Issued at 405 AM CDT Fri Jul 24 2026

Increased low level moisture will bring low clouds and perhaps
some patchy fog across south central and southeastern portions
this morning. Surface trough with broad ridging aloft will 
bring a few different weather impacts today. To start, SPC has 
maintained the Slight Risk for much of central and eastern ND, 
while expanded the Marginal Risk into most of the state except 
the southwest. Overall the setup remains similar to previous 
discussions. Surface trough will move through today, with a weak
cold front replacing a weak warm front this afternoon and 
evening. Modest instability and shear will be found along these 
fronts bringing all hazards of severe weather possible, if a 
stout cap can be broken. The likely main threat will be wind. 
Inverted V soundings, high DCAPE values, and modest to high 0 to
3 KM shear all indicate winds of 70 mph possible, with perhaps 
higher winds depending on what storm mode develops. Current 
thinking is storms are multi cluster today, with a brief window 
for supercells. Any supercells could bring large hail to golf 
ball in size. SPC has introduced an intensity level 1 for hail 
in the slight risk area, indicating hail 2 inches or greater is 
possible. This would be very conditional on rotating supercells 
and timing of the higher shear influencing these. This higher 
shear may be delayed to behind the surface trough, thus kept 
with golf ball sized hail for today. A tornado or two also 
remains possible although are still conditional on a surface 
based supercell storm mode and some interactions with either 
storms or remnant boundaries from this mornings convection if 
any. STP values around 1 are also found for a limited time this 
afternoon. Thus will maintain mention of a tornado or two 
possible, although chances still remain low. Timing wise, some 
thunderstorms are currently along the cold front in southern 
Canada. These thunderstorms could clip northern ND this morning,
although should remain elevated. As this front and surface 
trough moves through this afternoon and evening, look for better
chances of severe weather in central and eastern ND especially 
in the more moisture rich areas from this morning. This is again
assuming the cap can be broken today. The initial thunderstorms
should push eastward by early to mid evening. Some CAMs have 
isolated severe thunderstorms redeveloping along the stalled 
boundary later this evening into the early overnight hours. 
Although instability along this boundary lowers, shear will 
remain high. Chances for this redevelopment appear low at this 
time, although any sort of low level jet could be enough to 
overcome the lower lift along the stalled boundary thus have 
placed in some slight PoPs for this. 

The next areas of concern for today are hot temperatures and 
the potential for near critical fire weather conditions. Warm 
front moving through will bring warming temperatures forecast in
the 90s to lower 100s for much of the state today. However, 
HRRR smoke showing abundant wildfire smoke both aloft and at the
surface moving in by this afternoon and lingering through 
tonight. Local research suggests abundant vertically integrated 
smoke could impact temperatures 5 to 10 degrees. Forecast HRRR 
Vertically Integrated Smoke values today appear to be modest yet
may impact high temperatures, thus have lowered them a few 
degrees from the NBM. This lowering also lowers apparent 
temperatures today enough to create uncertainty on heat products
for today. Thus will hold off, although some south central 
areas will get close to heat index values near 100 degrees. 
These hot and dry conditions, combined with increased westerly 
winds from the mentioned front could bring some near critical 
fire weather conditions to southwestern and south central 
portions this afternoon and evening. The number of hours of 
these near critical conditions combined with reported partially 
green fuels has cause to hold off on any fire weather products 
as well for today.

This weekend, hot temperatures and dangerous heat remains the
biggest concern. Stalled front lifts back north Saturday, while
the upper level ridge also looks to rebound slightly. This could
be the hottest day of the weekend, although may depend on how
much wildfire smoke lingers across the area. Widespread
temperatures forecast in the 100s could lead to dangerous heat
index values also in the 100s. Still appears to be a dryer heat
compared to last weekend, although could still at least hit
advisory levels. Although confidence is increasing in a heat
product for this weekend, would still like to see how smoke
impacts temperatures today, which could play out similar this
weekend. Even so, those with outdoor plans will want to use
caution given the elevated potential for dangerous heat this
weekend. Weak instability, surface low, and the mentioned
boundary could bring afternoon and evening thunderstorms each
